name: White rice
description: The staple grain of three of our four cuisines.

unani.note: Chawal is classically thanda — hence 'rice at night makes you cold' folk advice.

histamine.note: Safest staple — but eat freshly cooked; refrigerated leftover rice accumulates amines.

name: Brown rice
description: Whole-bran rice, chewier and slower.

ayurveda.note: Heavier and slightly more heating than white.

name: Sticky rice
description: Chewy glutinous rice of zongzi and desserts.

tcm.note: Unusual among rices — TCM calls it warming and heavy.

nutrition.highlight: chewy enough to be filling in half the portion

name: Wheat flour (atta/maida)
description: The flour behind roti, khubz, noodles, and bread.

tcm.note: TCM calls wheat cooling — the direct opposite of the desi view.

unani.note: Gehun is classically garam — wheat halwa is winter food.

histamine.note: Modest; yeasted/fermented breads add a little more.

name: White bread
description: Yeasted everyday loaf.

histamine.note: Yeast adds a small load; sourdough is worse (fermented).

nutrition.highlight: carbohydrate with the bran taken out

name: Oats
description: Breakfast porridge grain.

histamine.note: A safe breakfast for histamine-sensitive people.

nutrition.highlight: the beta-glucan is what makes porridge thick

name: Barley
description: Ancient cooling grain; the base of jau ka pani and Prophetic talbina.

unani.note: THE classic cooling grain of Unani — barley water for heat.

nutrition.highlight: cooling in a way no other grain is said to be

name: Millet (bajra)
description: Hardy winter flatbread grain.

tcm.note: TCM's xiao mi (foxtail millet) is cooling — a different millet from bajra.

ayurveda.note: Bajra is textbook garam — a winter roti.

nutrition.highlight: gluten-free, and iron-rich for a grain

name: Sorghum (jowar)
description: Mild gluten-free flatbread grain.

ayurveda.note: Folk calls jowar thanda (summer roti), some texts say neutral-warm.

name: Semolina (sooji)
description: Coarse wheat middlings of halwa, upma, and harissa cake.

tcm.note: Follows TCM wheat.

unani.note: Follows wheat's garam nature; sooji halwa is a warming dish.

nutrition.highlight: coarse enough to toast before it cooks

name: Quinoa
description: Protein-rich Andean pseudo-grain.

tcm.note: New-world; inferred.

ayurveda.note: Light, dry, mildly heating per modern Ayurvedic use.

nutrition.highlight: one of the few plant foods with all nine amino acids

name: Couscous
description: Tiny steamed wheat pearls.

tcm.note: Follows TCM wheat; thin documentation.

name: Bulgur
description: Parboiled cracked wheat of tabbouleh and kibbeh.

tcm.note: Follows TCM wheat.

nutrition.highlight: already parboiled, so it only needs soaking

name: Pasta
description: Durum wheat noodles, Italian style.

histamine.note: Plain pasta fine — the sauces (tomato, aged cheese) are the problem.

nutrition.highlight: durum holds its shape where soft wheat collapses

name: Rice noodles
description: Soft gluten-free noodles of pho and chow fun.

nutrition.highlight: gluten-free by nature, not by substitution

name: Wheat noodles
description: Chewy wheat noodles of chow mein and la mian.

histamine.note: As wheat; watch the sauces more than the noodle.

nutrition.highlight: chew comes from gluten, not from cooking

name: Cornmeal (makki atta)
description: Ground corn; makki di roti and polenta.

tcm.note: Follows corn.

unani.note: Makki roti is the classic winter pairing with sarson saag.

nutrition.highlight: gluten-free, and it must be stirred

name: Buckwheat (kuttu)
description: Nutty pseudo-grain; kuttu atta of fasting days.

ayurveda.note: Called heating in Ayurveda — used in vrat (fasting) food; disagrees with TCM.

nutrition.highlight: not wheat at all, despite the name

name: Besan
description: Ground chana — the batter for pakora, the thickener for kadhi.

tcm.note: Follows the chickpea, which has no strong Chinese classification.

ayurveda.note: Chanaka is shita and ruksha (drying) — cooling but wind-forming.

unani.note: Besan is thanda in desi usage, which is why it is used on the skin against heat rash.

histamine.note: Low as a flour. Fermented besan batters are a different matter.

name: Atta
description: Stoneground whole wheat — the flour every roti starts from.

tcm.note: Follows wheat, which TCM reads as cool and heart-calming.

ayurveda.note: Godhuma is shita, guru and snigdha — building and cooling.

unani.note: Gehun is garam-tar in desi Unani usage — the exact opposite of the Chinese reading.

histamine.note: Low; wheat's issue for most people is gluten, not histamine.

nutrition.highlight: the flour every roti starts from

name: Maida
description: White flour with the bran and germ stripped out — naan, cake, samosa pastry.

tcm.note: Read with wheat; refining removes fibre, not nature.

ayurveda.note: Shita like wheat, but far more guru and abhishyandi (channel-clogging) once refined.

unani.note: Garam-tar and heavy, held to sit in the stomach.

name: Rice flour
description: Ground rice — the crispness in a dosa, the body in a rice noodle.

tcm.note: Follows rice, which is neutral and spleen-strengthening.

ayurveda.note: Shita like the grain it comes from.

histamine.note: Very low — rice is the standard safe base on a reactive day.

name: Poha
description: Rice parboiled and rolled flat — soaks in seconds, cooks in minutes.

tcm.note: Read with rice.

ayurveda.note: Shita and laghu — lighter than cooked rice, which is why it is a breakfast food.

unani.note: Thanda, and easy on the stomach.

name: Puffed rice
description: Rice exploded dry into weightless puffs — the body of every bhel.

tcm.note: Read with rice; dry-puffing adds a drying quality.

ayurveda.note: Laghu and shita — about the lightest form rice takes.

name: Seviyan
description: Fine roasted wheat threads — sweetened into kheer, or fried into upma.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

ayurveda.note: Shita like wheat, though roasting lightens it.

unani.note: Garam like gehun, and the Eid sheer khurma is built on it.

name: Roti
description: Unleavened wholewheat flatbread, puffed straight on the flame.

tcm.note: Follows wheat, tempered by dry-cooking.

ayurveda.note: Shita like the atta it is made from, and light because it is unleavened.

unani.note: Garam like gehun, though far lighter than fried breads.

histamine.note: Low; no yeast and no fermentation.

name: Naan
description: Leavened white-flour bread slapped onto the wall of a tandoor.

tcm.note: Leavened and fiercely dry-baked — warmer than a plain flatbread.

ayurveda.note: Fermented dough turns wheat's shita, the same logic that makes leavened bread heating.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; maida plus yeast plus tandoor heat.

histamine.note: Yeast-leavened and often enriched with yogurt — both push it above an unleavened roti.

nutrition.highlight: leavened, then blistered in a tandoor

name: Pita
description: Round leavened bread that puffs into a hollow pocket in the oven.

tcm.note: Read with white bread.

ayurveda.note: Leavened wheat, so ushna — like other yeasted breads.

unani.note: Garam; the daily bread of the Levantine table.

histamine.note: Yeast-leavened, so it sits with the other risen breads rather than with flatbreads.

name: Sourdough
description: Bread risen slowly on a wild starter instead of packet yeast.

tcm.note: Fermentation is read as warming; the base grain is wheat.

ayurveda.note: A long sour ferment is firmly ushna — sourness is the marker.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, more so than a quickly risen loaf.

histamine.note: A long wild ferment builds histamine, though SIGHI itself hedges on very long-proved sourdough rather than ruling it out — treat as uncertain, not settled.

name: Rye bread
description: Dense dark loaf, usually soured, with a sharp malty edge.

tcm.note: Read with the cooling cereal grains.

ayurveda.note: The souring dominates; no classical entry for rye.

unani.note: Placed with the drying grains; outside the classical record.

histamine.note: Nearly always sour-risen; the same open question SIGHI raises about long-proved sourdough applies here.

name: Tortilla
description: Thin unleavened round of corn or wheat, cooked on a dry griddle.

tcm.note: Follows corn, which is neutral, or wheat if wheat-based.

ayurveda.note: Unleavened and read with its base grain.

histamine.note: Low unleavened; the shelf-stable packs carry preservatives, which is a separate question.

name: Rye
description: Hardy dark grain that grows where wheat won't — malty and dense.

tcm.note: Grouped with the cooling cereals; not in the classical Chinese record.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; read with the grain family.

histamine.note: Low as a whole grain; it is the sour breads made from it that climb.

name: Spelt
description: An older wheat species — nuttier, and often better tolerated.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

ayurveda.note: Follows godhuma; no separate classical entry.

histamine.note: Low; still gluten-bearing, which is a separate sensitivity.

name: Farro
description: Chewy ancient wheat berries, simmered into salads and soups.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

name: Black rice
description: Deep purple whole-grain rice that stains everything it's cooked with.

tcm.note: Hei mi is warmer than white rice — a blood- and kidney-tonifying grain in the Chinese reading.

ayurveda.note: Regional rather than classical; read with rice.

nutrition.highlight: the purple is anthocyanin, same as blueberries

name: Red rice
description: Unpolished rice with a red bran layer — coarse, nutty, filling.

tcm.note: Read with rice; the intact bran adds a warming, moving quality.

ayurveda.note: Shita like rice, but heavier and slower with the bran left on.

name: Udon
description: Thick soft white wheat noodles, served in broth or fried.

tcm.note: A wheat noodle, so it follows wheat's cool reading.

ayurveda.note: Read with wheat; no classical entry.

histamine.note: Low plain; the broth it sits in usually matters more.

name: Soba
description: Brown buckwheat noodles, eaten hot in broth or cold with dipping sauce.

tcm.note: Qiao mai is cool and descending — traditionally eaten in summer, and held back in cold conditions.

histamine.note: Low. Buckwheat is a common allergen, which is a separate mechanism from histamine.

name: Sabudana
description: Translucent starch pearls soaked till they swell — the vrat khichdi staple.

tcm.note: Read with the starches; neutral and spleen-strengthening.

ayurveda.note: Shita and guru — pure starch, and the reason it is permitted on fasting days.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; heavy and filling, easy on a fasting stomach.

histamine.note: Very low — nearly pure starch, and among the safest things on a reactive day.

name: Singhara atta
description: Flour ground from dried water chestnuts — a fasting-day flour, not a cereal at all.

tcm.note: Follows water chestnut, which is cold and heat-clearing.

ayurveda.note: Shita; permitted on vrat precisely because it is not a grain.

name: Rajgira
description: Tiny amaranth seeds, popped into laddu or ground for fasting-day rotis.

tcm.note: No classical Chinese entry for the grain.

ayurveda.note: Shita and light; a permitted fasting pseudo-grain.

name: Samak rice
description: Tiny millet grains cooked like rice on fasting days.

tcm.note: Read with the millets, which are neutral to cool.

ayurveda.note: Shita and laghu — light enough for a fast.

name: Ragi
description: Dark red millet, ground into flour for mudde, roti and malt.

tcm.note: Read with the millets — cooling and drying.

ayurveda.note: Shita and ruksha; a summer grain in the south, though eaten year-round.

unani.note: Thanda-khushk, which is why it is cooked with warming tempering.

name: Foxtail millet
description: The millet of northern Chinese congee and South Indian upma alike.

tcm.note: Xiao mi is cool and strengthens the spleen and stomach — the classical congee grain for a weak digestion.

name: Little millet
description: A small quick-cooking millet, used where rice would be.

tcm.note: Grouped with the millets.

name: Freekeh
description: Young green wheat roasted over fire while still moist — smoky and chewy.

tcm.note: Read with wheat; the fire-roasting adds warmth.

unani.note: Garam like gehun in the Levantine reading.

name: Jowar flour
description: Sorghum ground for bhakri — gluten-free, and it will not hold together like wheat.

tcm.note: Read with sorghum, which is cooling.

ayurveda.note: Shita and ruksha; the classic summer roti flour of the Deccan.

unani.note: Thanda-khushk; eaten in the hot months for exactly that reason.

name: Oat flour
description: Oats milled fine — used in bakes and as a thickener.

tcm.note: Follows oats, which are neutral and strengthening.

ayurveda.note: Read with oats: guru, snigdha and mildly ushna.

name: Breadcrumbs
description: Dried bread ground coarse — the coating on everything fried.

tcm.note: Read with the bread it is made from.

histamine.note: Made from yeasted bread, so it carries that; usually fried on top.

name: Instant noodles
description: Wheat noodles flash-fried and dried, with a sachet of seasoning.

tcm.note: Fried and dried; warmer than a plain wheat noodle.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: refined wheat, fried in palm oil, with a salt-heavy masala.

histamine.note: The seasoning sachet is the problem, not the noodle. Yeast extract is both high in biogenic amines and a documented DAO inhibitor, so it blocks the enzyme that would clear them.

name: Bagel
description: Dough boiled before baking, which is what gives the dense chew.

tcm.note: Leavened and twice-cooked.

histamine.note: Yeast-leavened, like the other risen breads.

name: Croissant
description: Laminated dough folded around butter dozens of times, then proved and baked.

tcm.note: Rich, fermented and baked — warming and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru: refined flour, butter and a long ferment.

histamine.note: Yeasted and butter-rich; the long cold proof adds to it.

name: Filo pastry
description: Paper-thin unleavened sheets brushed with fat and stacked — the shell of baklava.

tcm.note: Unleavened wheat sheets; read with wheat.

ayurveda.note: Follows wheat; unleavened, so lighter than risen breads.

unani.note: Garam like gehun, and always cooked in fat.

histamine.note: Low — unleavened, unlike most bakery wheat.

name: Puff pastry
description: Layers of dough and fat that separate and rise in the oven without any yeast.

tcm.note: Fat-rich and baked hot.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru; refined flour and a great deal of fat.

histamine.note: Low — no yeast, unlike the risen breads. Commercial versions use palm fat.

name: Crackers
description: Thin dry baked wheat — the shelf-stable snack base.

tcm.note: Dry-baked wheat; read with wheat.

ayurveda.note: Ruksha and ushna from the baking.

histamine.note: Low plain; flavoured and cheese versions inherit those triggers.

name: Rusk
description: Bread baked twice until it is dry all the way through — dunked in chai.

tcm.note: Twice-baked and very dry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and ruksha; leavened, then dried.

unani.note: Garam-khushk in a high degree — about as drying as bread gets.

histamine.note: Made from yeasted bread and dried, which concentrates rather than removes.

name: Rice vermicelli
description: Fine rice-flour threads that need soaking rather than boiling.

tcm.note: Read with rice.

name: Glass noodles
description: Transparent threads from mung bean starch — slippery, and almost tasteless.

tcm.note: Read with mung bean, which is cold and heat-clearing.

name: Broken rice
description: Rice cracked in milling — cooks fast and breaks down, which is why congee uses it.

tcm.note: Read with rice.

ayurveda.note: Shita and laghu; broken grains digest faster still.

name: Wheat bran
description: The outer husk sifted out of white flour, added back for fibre.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

ayurveda.note: Ruksha and shita — very drying and fibrous.

name: Wild rice
description: Long black grass seeds, not a rice at all — chewy and nutty.

tcm.note: Not the classical Chinese grain despite the name.

name: Job's tears
description: Round white grains simmered in soups — a damp-draining staple of Chinese diet therapy.

tcm.note: Yi yi ren is cool and drains damp; one of the most-used food-grade drugs in TCM.

name: Glutinous rice flour
description: Flour from sticky rice — chewy and stretchy, never crumbly.

tcm.note: Nuo mi is warm and binding, unlike ordinary rice.

ayurveda.note: Guru and harder to digest than plain rice.

name: Tapioca flour
description: Fine white starch from cassava — the chew in bubble tea pearls and gluten-free bakes.

tcm.note: Read with cassava.

name: Teff
description: The world's smallest grain, fermented into injera.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

histamine.note: Very low as the grain; fermenting it into injera is another matter.

name: Kamut
description: A large ancient wheat with a buttery flavour and more protein than modern kinds.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

name: Corn flakes
description: Milled corn rolled, toasted and usually sugared — the packet breakfast.

tcm.note: Read with corn; heavily processed.

ayurveda.note: Ruksha and ushna from the toasting.

histamine.note: Low; the fortification and sugar are the real story, not histamine.

name: Muesli
description: Raw oats with dried fruit, nuts and seeds — soaked overnight, or eaten dry.

tcm.note: Read with oats and dried fruit.

ayurveda.note: Nuts and dried fruit are ushna.

histamine.note: The dried fruit and nuts carry it, not the oats.

name: Lavash
description: Very thin unleavened bread baked against a hot wall, soft fresh and cracker-crisp dry.

tcm.note: Unleavened wheat; read with wheat.

name: Markook
description: Paper-thin bread cooked on a domed metal saj, folded around anything.

tcm.note: Unleavened wheat.

name: Injera
description: Spongy sour flatbread from teff batter fermented for days.

tcm.note: Read with teff; the ferment warms it.

ayurveda.note: A long sour ferment is ushna.

histamine.note: Days of wild fermentation — one of the most heavily fermented breads there is.

name: Baguette
description: Long crusty white loaf, meant to be eaten the day it is baked.

tcm.note: Read with white bread.

name: Brioche
description: Bread enriched with so much egg and butter it is nearly a cake.

tcm.note: Rich, fermented and baked.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru — egg, butter and a long proof.

histamine.note: Yeasted and egg-rich; the egg adds a liberator.

name: Pretzel
description: Dough dipped in alkaline solution before baking, which is what makes the crust.

tcm.note: Baked and salted.

nutrition.highlight: the lye bath makes the crust

name: Matzo
description: Flour and water baked flat in under eighteen minutes so it cannot rise.

tcm.note: Unleavened wheat.

histamine.note: Low — deliberately unfermented, which is the entire point of it.

name: Papad
description: Thin seasoned lentil wafers, roasted on a flame or fried until they blister.

tcm.note: Dry-roasted and salty.

ayurveda.note: Urad and hing are ushna; the salt adds to it.

unani.note: Garam-khushk in a high degree — very salty and drying.

histamine.note: Salt- and alkali-cured before drying, which is what lifts it above plain dal.

nutrition.highlight: roasted, or fried till it blisters

name: Sev
description: Fried besan noodles, fine or thick — the crunch on every chaat.

tcm.note: Deep-fried and spiced.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree — fried besan with chilli.

histamine.note: Fried and stored for weeks; the oil ages more than the besan does.

name: Rice cake
description: Pounded glutinous rice in dense chewy sticks or discs.

tcm.note: Read with glutinous rice — warm and binding.

name: Wonton wrapper
description: Thin squares of egg-and-wheat dough for wrapping and boiling.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

histamine.note: Egg in the dough carries a liberator flag.

name: Spring roll wrapper
description: Paper-thin sheets of wheat or rice for wrapping and frying.

tcm.note: Read with its base grain.

ayurveda.note: Shita if rice-based, cooler than wheat.

name: Sushi rice
description: Short-grain rice dressed while warm with vinegar, sugar and salt.

tcm.note: Rice with vinegar; the vinegar warms an otherwise neutral grain.

ayurveda.note: Shukta makes it ushna despite the shita rice beneath.

unani.note: Garam by the sirka, thanda by the rice — the dressing decides it.

histamine.note: Vinegar-dressed and held at room temperature, which is the whole technique and also the risk.

name: Somen
description: Hair-thin wheat noodles served ice-cold with dipping sauce in summer.

tcm.note: Read with wheat; eaten cold, in the heat.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; grouped with gehun.

name: Ramen noodles
description: Wheat noodles made springy with alkaline salts — that is what makes them ramen.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

ayurveda.note: The kansui alkali is kshara, classically ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Low plain; the broth and toppings decide the bowl.

nutrition.highlight: the alkali is what makes them ramen

name: Shirataki
description: Translucent konjac noodles with essentially no calories.

tcm.note: Read with konnyaku, which is cold in the Chinese record.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with konjac.

name: Harusame
description: Fine translucent starch noodles used in salads and hotpot.

tcm.note: Read with mung bean starch, which is cooling.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with the starch noodles.

name: Panko
description: Coarse airy crumbs from crustless bread — they fry lighter than ordinary breadcrumbs.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with bread.

name: Garaetteok
description: Cylinders of pounded rice, sliced for soup or left whole for tteokbokki.

tcm.note: Read with glutinous rice — warm and binding.

name: Dangmyeon
description: Springy translucent noodles from sweet potato starch — the noodle in japchae.

tcm.note: Read with sweet potato; a plain starch noodle.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with the starch noodles.

name: Chapssal
description: Sticky short-grain rice used for tteok and porridge.

tcm.note: Nuo mi is warm and binding.

nutrition.highlight: stickier than sticky rice, which is the point

name: Mung bean flour
description: Starch from mung beans, used to set puddings and make glass noodles.

tcm.note: Read with mung bean, which is cold and heat-clearing.

name: Black glutinous rice
description: Deep purple sticky rice simmered into sweet porridge with coconut milk.

tcm.note: Read with black rice and glutinous rice — both warming.

name: Banh pho
description: Flat fresh rice noodles, the width decided by which soup they are going into.

tcm.note: Read with rice.

nutrition.highlight: the width tells you the soup

name: Bun noodles
description: Thin round rice noodles served cool in bowls and salads, never in hot broth.

tcm.note: Rice noodles, served cool.

name: Hominy
description: Corn soaked in lime until the hulls slip off — the step that makes maize nourishing.

tcm.note: Read with corn; the alkaline soak is drying.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; the nixtamal process has no classical parallel.

name: Masa harina
description: Flour ground from hominy — what tortillas and tamales are made from.

tcm.note: Read with corn.

name: Arepa flour
description: Pre-cooked corn flour that hydrates instantly — arepas and nothing else.

tcm.note: Read with corn.

name: Farofa
description: Cassava flour toasted in butter — scattered over feijoada for texture.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with cassava; the toasting warms it.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; ushna from the toasting and fat.

name: Sangak
description: Long sourdough flatbread baked directly on hot stones, which leave dimples.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

name: Barbari
description: Thick ridged bread glazed before baking so the crust goes glossy.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

nutrition.highlight: the ridges are pressed by hand

name: Taftoon
description: A thin soft round bread baked fast against the oven wall.

tcm.note: Read with wheat.

name: Kadayıf
description: Pastry extruded into fine threads — the base of künefe and many syrup sweets.

tcm.note: Read with wheat pastry.

name: Garri
description: Cassava grated, fermented, pressed and toasted into granules — soaked cold or made into eba.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with cassava; the ferment adds warmth.

histamine.note: Cassava is deliberately fermented for days before toasting — that is what makes it garri, and what rates it.

name: Attiéké
description: Fermented grated cassava steamed into fine grains — Ivorian, and eaten with fish.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with cassava.

name: Kocho
description: Fermented enset pulp buried in a pit for months and baked flat.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; no classical entry; a long ferment.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; fermented, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment.

name: Jiu niang
description: Glutinous rice fermented a few days into a sweet boozy porridge, spooned into soup.

tcm.note: A warming rice ferment; used to move blood after childbirth.

histamine.note: A live ferment with alcohol in it.

name: Mung bean jelly
description: Mung bean starch set into a translucent block, sliced cold and dressed in chilli and vinegar.

tcm.note: Mung bean starch, served cold — a summer food.

histamine.note: Low on its own; the vinegar dressing is what rates.

name: Rumali roti
description: A bread stretched so thin it is cooked over an upturned pan and folded like cloth.

tcm.note: Plain thin wheat bread.

nutrition.highlight: folded like cloth, and named for it

name: Missi roti
description: Wheat and gram flour kneaded with onion and ajwain into a savoury flatbread.

tcm.note: Spiced flatbread with gram flour.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the ajwain and onion.

nutrition.highlight: savoury before anything goes on it

name: Sheermal
description: A slightly sweet saffron-milk bread, brushed with ghee and baked in a tandoor.

tcm.note: Enriched leavened bread.

name: Taftan
description: A soft milk-and-egg bread scattered with nigella and baked against the oven wall.

tcm.note: Enriched leavened bread.

name: Bakarkhani
description: A thick layered biscuit-bread, sometimes sweet, that keeps for days.

tcm.note: Layered enriched bread.

histamine.note: Low; it keeps because it is dry, not because it is cured.

nutrition.highlight: it keeps for days, and does

name: Rogni roti
description: Wheat dough enriched with milk and ghee, thicker and softer than a plain roti.

tcm.note: Enriched flatbread.

ayurveda.note: Ghrita and wheat together are guru.

nutrition.highlight: thicker and softer than a roti
